entries.title: modules
entries.summary: Splitting a program into .h and .c files.
entries.syntax:
util.h: types + prototypes (with an include guard)
util.c: #include "util.h" + the implementation
entries.description: The header is the interface; the source file implements it and includes its own header so the compiler checks both agree. Names that are internal to the module are `static`. Each `.c` is compiled separately into a `.o` and the linker joins them. Never define variables or functions in a header that several files include.
mistakes: Defining (not just declaring) a function in a header.

entries.title: gcc
entries.description: Stages: preprocessing, compilation, assembly, linking; by default gcc does all of them.

details.name: -c
details.text: compile to an object file (`a.c` → `a.o`), do not link

details.name: -Wall -Wextra
details.text: enable the useful warnings; fix every one

entries.example:
gcc -Wall -Wextra -g main.c util.c -o prog
gcc -c util.c -o util.o
gcc main.o util.o -o prog
mistakes: Ignoring warnings: most are real bugs.
Putting `-lm` before the source file (libraries go last).

entries.title: ar
entries.description: Packs object files into `libname.a`. The linker copies only the parts a program uses. `r` adds or replaces files, `c` creates the archive quietly, `s` writes an index.
entries.example:
gcc -c a.c b.c
ar rcs libutil.a a.o b.o
gcc main.c -L. -lutil -o prog
mistakes: Listing a dependent library before the one it needs.

entries.title: ld
entries.summary: The linker (gcc calls it for you).
entries.description: Joins object files and libraries into an executable or, with `-shared`, a dynamic library. In practice use `gcc -shared -fPIC -o libname.so a.c b.c`, which also takes care of position-independent code.
entries.example:
gcc -shared -fPIC -o libutil.so a.c b.c
gcc main.c -L. -lutil -o prog
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=. ./prog

entries.title: ldd
entries.summary: List the dynamic libraries a program needs.
entries.description: Shows each `.so` and where the loader finds it; `not found` means the loader cannot locate it (set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` or install the library).

entries.title: make
entries.summary: Rebuild only what changed, following a Makefile.
entries.description: `make target` runs the recipe of a rule when the target does not exist or a dependency is newer. Recipe lines MUST start with a TAB. Variables (`CC = gcc`, `CFLAGS = -Wall -g`) are used as `$(CC)`. A pattern rule such as `%.o: %.c` explains how to build any object from its source; in a recipe `$<` is the first dependency, `$^` all of them and `$@` the target. A target that is not a file (like `clean`) is declared with `.PHONY`.
entries.example:
CC = gcc
CFLAGS = -Wall -Wextra -g

prog: main.o util.o
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $^ -o $@

%.o: %.c
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

.PHONY: clean
clean:
	rm -f *.o prog
mistakes: Using spaces instead of a TAB.
Forgetting `-c` in the rule that builds an object file.

entries.title: man
entries.summary: Read the manual page of a function or command.
entries.description: Section 1 is commands, 2 system calls, 3 library functions. `man 2 open` is the system call, `man 3 printf` the library function. Inside: `/text` searches, `n` next match, `q` quits. The synopsis shows the headers to include.

details.name: man 2 name
details.text: system calls: open, read, write, dup2, chdir…

details.name: man 3 name
details.text: library functions: printf, fopen, strcmp, malloc…
